content: 1. Reduce the extent and rate of oral medications that require rapid gastrointestinal absorption. 2. Advise patients to take oral contraceptives at least one hour before administering exenatide. 3. Monitor closely the interaction between ethinylestradiol and exenatide injectable suspension. 4. Oral contraceptives may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. 5. Exenatide’s effect on slowing gastric emptying may reduce the absorption of oral medications requiring rapid GI absorption. 6. Fedratinib increases the level or effect of norethindrone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Fedratinib increases the level or effect of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Ethinylestradiol increases the level or effect of fedratinib. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Avoid coadministration of fedratinib (a CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 substrate) with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors. 10. Felbamate decreases levels of ethinylestradiol by an unknown mechanism. Monitor closely. 11. Fexinidazole increases the level or effect of norethindrone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4 and increases the level or effect of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Co-administration of fexinidazole may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 14. Ethinylestradiol increases the level or effect of fezolinetant by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Fezolinetant’s AUC and peak plasma concentration are increased when coadministered with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors. 16. Ethinylestradiol increases the level or effect of finerenone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 17. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 18. Ethinylestradiol increases the level or effect of flibanserin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Increased flibanserin adverse effects may occur if coadministered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Fluconazole increases the level or effect of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Ethinylestradiol increases the level or effect of fluvoxamine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Fosphenytoin decreases the level or effect of norethindrone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Hormonal contraceptives are not a reliable method of effective birth control when coadministered with fosphenytoin. 24. Ethinylestradiol increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the level or effect of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Istradefylline increases the level or effect of norethindrone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Istradefylline increases the level or effect of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Itraconazole increases the level or effect of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Ivosidenib decreases the level or effect of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Ivosidenib decreases the level or effect of norethindrone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Ketoconazole increases the level or effect of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Norethindrone decreases the level or effect of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor. 33. Ethinylestradiol decreases levels of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor. 34. Ethinylestradiol increases the level or effect of lapatinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 35. Larotrectinib increases the level or effect of norethindrone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 36. Larotrectinib increases the level or effect of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 37. Ethinylestradiol increases the level or effect of lemborexant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Lenacapavir increases the level or effect of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 39. Lenacapavir increases the level or effect of norethindrone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 41. Leniolisib increases the level or effect of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Lesinurad decreases the effect of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Lesinurad decreases the effect of norethindrone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Use additional methods of nonhormonal contraception when using lesinurad.
